name: Mother Ione
epithet: Of Saint Ysolde's; told of the riders
appearance: Not yet seen on the page, only named. When the grey cloaks were sighted on the Holloway, hers was the name the news went to first: "Mother Ione's been told." Her face and her bearing wait for the day she steps onto the page.
last_seen_doing: Not on the page herself: named by Wren Ashdown, who told the infirmary hall that Mother Ione had been told of the riders on the Holloway.
now: Told of the riders, as far as the reader knows: six grey cloaks and a cart on the Holloway road, a censer smoking in the snow, expected at the foot of the Steps by tomorrow night if the snow holds off. What she means to do is not yet on the page.
story_so_far: Mother Ione has not yet appeared in the Chronicle. On the morning the first snow came to Saint Ysolde's, Wren Ashdown came into the infirmary hall out of breath with news from the bell tower: six riders and a cart on the Holloway, grey cloaks, a censer smoking in the snow, and Mother Ione had been told. There is a list, read out at the inn in Coldmere and passed from a carter to the lay brothers to the kitchen, so that now everyone knows: the names of the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's, the ones the riders have come to bring down to kneel.

known_facts.fact: By the time Wren Ashdown reached the infirmary hall with word of the grey cloaks on the Holloway, Mother Ione had been told.
